summary: The Anne van den Ban Fund pays tuition, a living allowance, travel, visa and insurance for the full two years of a Wageningen University MSc. It is for students from 64 developing countries, among them Ghana, Kenya, Nigeria, Ethiopia and India. You cannot apply directly: Wageningen invites candidates from the complete MSc applications it receives before 1 December 2026.
meta_title: Anne van den Ban Fund 2027: full Wageningen MSc scholarship
meta_description: Wageningen's Anne van den Ban Fund pays tuition, living costs, travel and insurance for students from 64 countries. Apply for your MSc before 1 December 2026.
covers: Tuition fees for the 24 months of the MSc.
Travel to and from the Netherlands.
eligibility: Nationals of the 64 developing countries on Wageningen's list, including Ghana, Kenya, Nigeria, Ethiopia, Uganda, India and Pakistan.
Unconditional admission to a Wageningen MSc programme that starts in September 2027.
A bachelor's degree completed and uploaded before 1 December 2026, with official English test results available by then.
how_to_apply: There is no scholarship form. Submit a complete application for a Wageningen MSc that starts in September 2027 before 1 December 2026.
The Anne van den Ban selection committee assesses only the complete applications received before that date.
Wageningen tells the selected students during May 2027; the exact date has not been announced.
watch_out: The fund is awarded together with Wageningen's own WU Fellowship Programme.

Wageningen exempts only degrees taught in English on campus in Australia, Canada, Ireland, New Zealand, Singapore, South Africa, the UK or the US (and some Dutch qualifications). An English-taught degree from Ghana, Nigeria or Kenya does not exempt you, so sit IELTS Academic (6.5 overall, speaking 6.0) or TOEFL iBT (90, speaking 22) in time for the results to exist before 1 December 2026.
Citizens of African countries with a First Class degree and a GPA of 80% or higher are also considered for the Africa Scholarship Programme through the same application.
Wageningen's scholarships are for September starts only.
documents: A complete Wageningen MSc application, submitted before 1 December 2026
Your bachelor's diploma and transcripts, uploaded before 1 December 2026
Official IELTS or TOEFL results available before 1 December 2026

faq.q: Can I apply directly to the Anne van den Ban Fund?
faq.a: No. It is based on invitation. Submit a complete Wageningen MSc application before 1 December 2026 to be considered.

faq.q: Is Ghana eligible for the Anne van den Ban Fund?
faq.a: Yes. Ghana is one of the 64 countries on Wageningen's list, with Kenya, Nigeria, Ethiopia, Uganda, India and Pakistan.
Wageningen informs the selected students during May 2027.
